subject: Archaeology
title: Pseudoarchaeology: How to Spot It
description: A 60-second lesson on Pseudoarchaeology: How to Spot It.

hook.text: Lost continents, ancient energy grids, and giant civilizations — pseudoarchaeology thrives because real archaeology moves slowly.

buildup.text: Pseudoarchaeological claims ignore evidence, cherry-pick data, and present speculation as fact.

discovery.text: Common red flags: unnamed experts, no published research, claims that mainstream science is hiding the truth.

twist.text: Pseudoarchaeology often exploits real gaps in knowledge. Genuine mysteries attract fake explanations because answers are slow.

climax.text: The best defense is scientific literacy: checking sources, reading peer-reviewed papers.

punchline.text: If the explanation is exciting and requires no evidence, it is probably wrong.

quiz.question: What is a key red flag of pseudoarchaeological claims?
options: They are published in university journals
They claim mainstream science is hiding the truth and skip peer review
They focus on well-documented periods of history

details.summary: Pseudoarchaeology uses unscientific claims to explain the past — ancient aliens, lost civilizations, and supernatural builders. Real archaeology relies on testable evidence, peer review, and transparent methods. Learning to distinguish them protects public understanding of the human past.
details.whyItMatters: Pseudoarchaeology is popular because it offers exciting narratives, but it often denies ancient peoples credit for their achievements. Recognizing its hallmarks — lack of evidence, untestable claims — is essential for critical thinking.
takeaways: Pseudoarchaeology makes untestable or unfalsifiable claims
It often denies indigenous peoples credit for their achievements
Real archaeology relies on evidence, peer review, and transparency

faq.question: What are the warning signs of pseudoarchaeology?
faq.answer: Claims that invoke aliens, lost super-civilizations, or psychic knowledge. Refusal to submit evidence to peer review. Ignoring contradictory evidence. Suggesting mainstream archaeologists are conspiring to hide the truth. These are all red flags.

faq.question: Why is pseudoarchaeology harmful?
faq.answer: It erases indigenous achievements by attributing their monuments to aliens or lost white civilizations. It undermines public trust in science and diverts attention from genuine discoveries. The racist roots of many pseudoarchaeological claims are well documented.
